messages:
ops-app: morning all, our mobile users are reporting spikes of 429s and long tails on /v1/generate during the 07:15-07:35 UTC ramp. Behavior: some requests stall ~1-2s then a 429, others succeed. We're on hosted (rwd-3b), ~160 concurrent short lived sessions. Can someone triage? :grimacing:

sarah-support: sorry to hear this. Can you paste one failing request + response headers (token removed)? Also confirm whether your clients do instant retries. 429s usually mean quota/burst or a per-route throttle.

ops-app: sample curl below and headers we captured. We see `retry-after` in the response:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"Summarize this...","max_tokens":96}'
```

Response headers:
```
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 11
x-rw-burst-remaining: 0
x-rw-request-id: rwd-req-abc123
retry-after: 12
```

Body: `{\"error\":\"Rate limit exceeded\"}`

Note: our client retries immediately without jitter which creates request pileups on the client.

mike-runtime: two things to consider: (A) it looks like a quota/burst exhaustion (headers show remaining=0 + retry-after) and (B) compute spikes caused by continuous batching combined with very low KV-cache reuse can trigger tenant-level protective throttles. If every request has a different session key, KV cache hit rate -> 0 and per-call compute is higher.

ops-app: we do not set conversation_id or reuse session ids; each mobile request gets a random session uuid for privacy reasons.

lina-ml: that pattern kills KV reuse. KV cache helps avoid re-computing prefix attention states; misses multiply effective per-token work. With hundreds of ephemeral keys you lose those savings.

tara-support: also check whether you rely on server-side continuous batching default window. The runtime coalesces incoming requests within batch_window_ms (default 25ms). During traffic ramps, that can produce very large flushes and transient compute spikes.

ops-app: we use SDK defaults (server batching). We didn't tune batch_window_ms. Is lowering it recommended?

mike-runtime: options:
- reuse conversation_id scoped to the user or to a short-lived chat (e.g., per-30m). This increases KV cache hit rate.
- add jittered exponential backoff for retries; immediate retry storms amplify the pressure.
- tune batch_window_ms: if you're latency-sensitive, reduce to 5-10ms; if throughput matters, increase slightly but watch coalescing.
- if needed, request a temporary quota/burst uplift for the hot window while you roll changes.

Quick repro to simulate the problem locally (many ephemeral sessions + no convo id):

```
# pseudo load generator (Python)
for _ in range(1200):
    body = {"model":"rwd-3b","input":"Ping","max_tokens":64, "session_id": str(uuid4())}
    requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json=body, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer REDACTED"})
```

You should see 429s once token/quota thresholds are hit.

infra-bot: [ticket created] SUP-2044 linked.

mike-runtime: I pulled tenant metrics for your org (org-zz9):
- tokens in window: ~2.05M
- KV cache hit rate for that traffic: ~6%
- mean batch size at flush: 18, with bursts to 50 during spikes
- p99 batch flush latency: ~700-900ms during spikes
- throttle events line up with flushes having >30 requests

diagnosis: large flush spikes + near-zero KV hits -> sudden compute surge -> tenant burst limiter engages -> some requests get queued or 429. Client instant retries then worsen the transient.

tara-support: immediate remediation for your team:
- implement stable conversation_id reuse (e.g., derive from user id hashed) for a 15-60 min window to preserve privacy but enable KV reuse.
- implement randomized backoff for retries (use jitter, cap attempts).
- reduce batch_window_ms to ~8ms temporarily to reduce coalescing of small requests into huge flushes.
- request temporary burst increase (48h) while you deploy fixes.

ops-app: can you apply a temporary +2x burst for 48h? Also, is switching to rwd-1b a viable emergency option to reduce compute?

sarah-support: we can provision a temporary burst uplift for 48h; state requested headroom (1.5x, 2x, etc). Switching to rwd-1b lowers compute and cost but may affect response quality; preferred path is burst uplift + conversation_id reuse + backoff.

ops-app: please do +2x for 48h. We'll ship session reuse + jitter backoff within 5 hours.

mike-runtime: internal note: create runtime mitigation that if a tenant's KV hit rate < 30% and mean batch size > 20, cap that tenant's effective max_batch_size to reduce spike amplitude; file ENG-RUNTIME-901. That will limit flash spikes while teams fix client behavior.

lina-ml: implementation tip: when reusing conversation_id, avoid sending the whole chat history each call. Use a short prefix or a compacted summary and prefer prefix-KV-only mode so KV cache stays efficient without bloating context length.

ops-app: update ~5.5h later: deployed session_id reuse + jittered backoffs + lowered batch window. Observed KV hit rate rise to ~60% and 429s dropped to 0. p99 latency improved from ~900ms to ~210ms. Great result. :rocket:

rachel-sre: adding a runbook entry: "Perceived throttling from continuous batching + KV-cache misses". Include diagnostics: query per-org KV hit rate, batch size histogram, x-rw-rate-limit-* headers, and quick repro script. I'll open a runbook PR.

sarah-support: closing SUP-2044 for now; reopen if issues recur. :white_check_mark:
